name: Distributed Shared Virtual Memory Volume Rendering
aliases: Distributed shared virtual-memory scheme (Beyer et al.)
definition: A volume rendering system that uses a single virtual memory space shared by all rendering nodes and GPUs. Each node refers to the same shared 3D virtual memory space representing the entire volume, accessed independently on each GPU. Ray-casting on each GPU determines small 3D blocks (memory pages) actually accessed. Virtual memory is managed via a two-level hierarchy of page tables, and physical memory is only mapped for the current working set of pages.
summary: Distributed Shared Virtual Memory Volume Rendering renders tera-scale volumes on GPU clusters by mapping the entire dataset into a single shared virtual memory space, using on-demand paging and hardware-assisted page faults instead of explicit data partitioning.
